content.title: About
content.content: Plain muffin is a soft, mildly sweet quick‑bread made from wheat flour, eggs, milk, butter and a small amount of sugar. It has a tender crumb and a neutral flavor, making it an ideal base for a variety of toppings and fillings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Muffins originated in England in the 19th century as a way to use up leftover batter.
Traditional plain muffins are often split and toasted to create a crisp exterior.
In the United States plain muffins are commonly used as the base for eggs Benedict.
The batter requires minimal mixing, which helps keep the crumb light and airy.
There are many variations—blueberry, chocolate chip, nut, etc.—but the plain version remains the most versatile.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Muffins provide carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Eggs and milk add a modest amount of animal protein.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour and eggs supply B1, B2 and B6 vitamins, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: Milk contributes calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Low sodium
items.content: Plain muffins are typically made without added salt, making them suitable for moderate sodium intake.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat flour contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although plain muffins are not overly sweet, they do contain sugar, which may be a concern for diabetics or those monitoring weight.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Butter and eggs make the muffin relatively calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Trans fats from improper fat choice
items.content: Using margarine instead of butter can introduce trans fats, which are undesirable for cardiovascular health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Plain muffins can be enjoyed as a snack on their own, split and toasted with butter, jam, honey, or used as a base for sandwiches with ham, cheese, and vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store muffins in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer keeping, refrigerate (up to 5 days) or freeze (up to 2 months). Reheat in the oven or toaster before serving to restore a crisp crust.
